newsitem.title: USA: JFAX names Richard Ressler chief executive.
newsitem.headline: JFAX names Richard Ressler chief executive.

text.p: JFAX Personal Telecom, a private company that allows people to send faxes to and from electronic mailboxes, on Thursday said it named Richard Ressler to the new position of chief executive.
JFAX also said Michael Schulhof, the former chairman and president of Sony Corp North America, had become an active investor in the company.
Both men made "significant" investments of undisclosed amounts in JFAX, according to Jaye Muller, the company's president and founder.
Muller told Reuters the involvement and the investments of Ressler and Schulhof were a "next step" in the company's evolution, though he said there were no firm plans for an initial public offering.
"There are no direct dates. It is definitely something we are considering," he said.
The JFAX personal telecom technology converts faxes and automatically delivers them to an electronic mailbox or a fax machine. People are also able to receive voice mail with the technology.
Muller said JFAX allowed its customers, including business travelers and smaller operations, to select phone numbers from around the world and set up "virtual offices."
Ressler, most recently president and chief executive at MAI Systems Corp, will focus on an accelerated global rollout in the next quarter, Muller said.
The company's network includes 22 cities, with recent launches in Paris, Amsterdam, Vancouver, Toronto and Montreal.

"Richard Ressler's experience in repositioning global companies will push JFAX to establish true leadership in the industry," Muller said. "At the same time, Michael Schulhof's capital infusion and role as an active investor will help JFAX to establish important partnerships and relations with traditional and non-traditional business giants."
The company said it planned to double its staff within three months and open a co-headquarters in Los Angeles, which Ressler will oversee.
The research and development team and the operations and customer support departments will move to Los Angeles. The marketing and sales departments will remain in New York.
